title: Equivalence transport for invertible endofunctor fixed pairs
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be categories in a common sufficiently large universe [def-nagata-category], $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ and $G:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D$ endofunctors, $J:\mathcal C\simeq\mathcal D$ an equivalence, and $b:J\circ F\xrightarrow{\sim}G\circ J$ a natural isomorphism (ordinary composition notation). Use the fixed-pair categories [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category]. Then
$$\widetilde J:\mathcal C^F\simeq\mathcal D^G,\qquad (K,\theta)\longmapsto(JK,J(\theta)\circ b_K^{-1}),\quad u\longmapsto J(u)$$
is an equivalence with the displayed underlying functor. For any two source pairs, the Hom bijection of $\widetilde J$ is exactly the Hom bijection of $J$ restricted to intertwining arrows; explicitly, writing $\psi_K=J(\theta_K)b_K^{-1}$, for every $u:K\to K'$ one has
$$J(u)\psi_K=\psi_{K'}G(Ju)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad u\theta_K=\theta_{K'}F(u).$$
Moreover, for every target pair $(H,\psi)$ and every isomorphism $v:JK\xrightarrow{\sim}H$, the unique arrow $\theta:F K\to K$ whose $J$-image is $v^{-1}\psi G(v)b_K$ is invertible, with inverse the unique lift of $(v^{-1}\psi G(v)b_K)^{-1}$; $v$ is an isomorphism from $\widetilde J(K,\theta)$ to $(H,\psi)$. No equivalence assumption on $F$ or $G$ is required.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-quasi-inverse-hom-bijection] to the functor of $J$ and its quasi-inverse. Thus $u\mapsto J(u)$ is bijective on each Hom set; in particular $J$ is full and faithful. Write all compositions in ordinary order. Since $\theta_K$ and $b_K$ are invertible, $\psi_K=J(\theta_K)b_K^{-1}$ is invertible with inverse $b_KJ(\theta_K^{-1})$. Hence $(JK,\psi_K)$ is an object of the target fixed-pair category [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category].

source.place: Tag 02C3 (categories-lemma-equivalence-categories), equivalence implies full faithfulness; elementary inverse formula

proof.text:
For any $u:K\to K\prime$, naturality of $b$ reads $G(Ju)b_K=b_{K\prime}J(Fu)$. Consequently
$$J(u)\psi_K=J(u\theta_K)b_K^{-1},\qquad\psi_{K\prime}G(Ju)=J(\theta_{K\prime}Fu)b_K^{-1}.$$
Cancel $b_K^{-1}$ and use the injectivity established in step 1. This proves the displayed equivalence of intertwining equations for every $u$, in both directions.

source.place: Final coefficient-category sentence: explicit naturality calculation for fixed-pair transport

proof.text: By the morphism definition in [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category], step 2 makes $u\mapsto J(u)$ a map on fixed-pair morphisms. It preserves identities and composition because $J$ does, so together with step 1 it defines the displayed functor $\widetilde J$. Given a target intertwining arrow between two image objects, the Hom bijection in step 1 gives a unique $u$; step 2 says that this $u$ intertwines the source structures. Thus the Hom bijection of $\widetilde J$ is exactly the restriction of that of $J$ to intertwining arrows.

source.place: Final coefficient-category sentence: functoriality and restricted Hom bijection

proof.text: Fix any target pair $(H,\psi)$ and any isomorphism $v:JK\xrightarrow{\sim}H$. The composite $w=v^{-1}\psi G(v)b_K$ is an isomorphism $J(FK)\to JK$: an explicit inverse is $b_K^{-1}G(v^{-1})\psi^{-1}v$, since functors preserve compositions and identities. The functor $J$ is fully faithful by step 1, so [lem-cbc-fully-faithful-isomorphism-lift], applied to $FK,K$, gives a unique isomorphism $\theta:FK\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ with $J(\theta)=w$. By the Hom bijection in step 1 this is also the unique arrow with that image; and $J(\theta^{-1})=w^{-1}$, so its inverse is precisely the unique lift asserted in the statement.

source.place: Final coefficient-category sentence: lift the conjugated structure map, using FullyFaithful.isoEquiv (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Functor/FullyFaithful.lean:217)

proof.text:
For the lift in step 4, direct cancellation gives
$$v\psi_K=vJ(\theta)b_K^{-1}=\psi G(v).$$
Therefore $v$ is a fixed-pair morphism. Multiplying this equality by $v^{-1}$ on the left and $G(v^{-1})$ on the right gives $v^{-1}\psi=\psi_KG(v^{-1})$. Thus $v^{-1}$ is also a fixed-pair morphism; their composites are the identity arrows by [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category]. This proves the asserted fixed-pair isomorphism for every specified $v$.

source.place: Final coefficient-category sentence: check both directions of the lifted pair isomorphism

proof.text: For every $H$ choose $K=J^{-1}H$ and $v:JK\xrightarrow{\sim}H$ to be the component of the counit isomorphism of the given equivalence $J$. Steps 4 and 5 show that every target pair is isomorphic to an image pair. Step 3 proves bijectivity on Hom sets. Apply [lem-trf-fully-faithful-ess-surj-equivalence] (Stacks Tag 02C3, categories-lemma-equivalence-categories) to $\widetilde J$, in the common sufficiently large universe stipulated in the statement. It gives an equivalence with this very functor. None of the constructions or cancellations used an inverse functor for $F$ or $G$.

lean.statement: theorem fixedPair_equivalence_transport {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {D : Type u'} [Category.{v'} D] (F : C ⥤ C) (G : D ⥤ D) (J : C ≌ D) (b : F ⋙ J.functor ≅ J.functor ⋙ G) : (mapOfNatIso b.symm).IsEquivalence ∧ (∀ K : IsoAlgebra F, ((mapOfNatIso b.symm).obj K).carrier = J.functor.obj K.carrier ∧ ((mapOfNatIso b.symm).obj K).obj.str = b.inv.app K.carrier ≫ J.functor.map K.obj.str) ∧ (∀ (K K' : IsoAlgebra F) (f : K ⟶ K'), ((mapOfNatIso b.symm).map f).hom.f = J.functor.map f.hom.f) ∧ (∀ K K' : IsoAlgebra F, Function.Bijective ((mapOfNatIso b.symm).map : (K ⟶ K') → ((mapOfNatIso b.symm).obj K ⟶ (mapOfNatIso b.symm).obj K'))) ∧ (∀ (K K' : IsoAlgebra F) (u : K.carrier ⟶ K'.carrier), ((b.inv.app K.carrier ≫ J.functor.map K.obj.str) ≫ J.functor.map u = G.map (J.functor.map u) ≫ b.inv.app K'.carrier ≫ J.functor.map K'.obj.str) ↔ K.obj.str ≫ u = F.map u ≫ K'.obj.str) ∧ (∀ (H : IsoAlgebra G) (K : C) (v : J.functor.obj K ≅ H.carrier), ∃ θ : F.obj K ≅ K, (∀ t : F.obj K ⟶ K, J.functor.map t = b.hom.app K ≫ G.map v.hom ≫ H.obj.str ≫ v.inv ↔ t = θ.hom) ∧ (∀ t : K ⟶ F.obj K, J.functor.map t = v.hom ≫ H.str.inv ≫ G.map v.inv ≫ b.inv.app K ↔ t = θ.inv) ∧ ∃ e : (mapOfNatIso b.symm).obj (mk K θ) ≅ H, e.hom.hom.f = v.hom ∧ e.inv.hom.f = v.inv)
